title: Coadministration of a tumor-penetrating peptide enhances the efficacy of cancer drugs
central_claims: Unconjugated coadministration of iRGD increases tumor penetration and therapeutic efficacy of diverse anticancer drugs.

source_manifest.title: Replication Study: Coadministration of a tumor-penetrating peptide enhances the efficacy of cancer drugs.
source_manifest.finding: Direct prostate DOX experiment found no enhancement of penetration, tumor-weight reduction or apoptosis with iRGD.

source_manifest.title: Improving Drug Penetrability with iRGD Leverages the Therapeutic Response to Sorafenib and Doxorubicin in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
source_manifest.finding: Independent HCC models showed improved drug delivery and treatment with iRGD coadministration.

source_manifest.title: A Novel Strategy to Improve the Therapeutic Efficacy of Gemcitabine for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer by the Tumor-Penetrating Peptide iRGD.
source_manifest.finding: Independent A549 model found gemcitabine plus iRGD improved tumor inhibition over gemcitabine alone.

research.summary: Direct prostate DOX experiment found no enhancement of penetration, tumor-weight reduction or apoptosis with iRGD. Independent HCC models showed improved drug delivery and treatment with iRGD coadministration. Independent A549 model found gemcitabine plus iRGD improved tumor inhibition over gemcitabine alone.
